incentives.name: Industrial revenue bonds (IRBs) with property tax abatement
incentives.law: County Industrial Revenue Bond Act (NMSA 1978, 4-59-1 et seq.) and municipal Industrial Revenue Bond Act (NMSA 1978, 3-32-1 et seq.)
incentives.what: County or city issues bonds and holds title to the land and equipment, leasing it back to the company, so the project pays no property tax except a negotiated PILOT. Used for Project Jupiter (~$165B, 95% abatement, $12M/yr PILOT for 30 years), Meta Los Lunas (Village IRBs) and proposed for Google Lea County (~$134B).
incentives.value_known: Project Jupiter: EDD estimates current property tax on the land ~$55,427/yr vs. $360M PILOT over 30 years

incentives.name: Local Economic Development Act (LEDA) gross receipts tax share
incentives.law: Local Economic Development Act, NMSA 1978, 5-10-1 et seq.
incentives.what: For projects over $350M in construction costs, 50% of general-fund GRT paid on construction can be returned to the project through the LEDA fund if the state, county and city all agree. Meta Los Lunas also received $10M in LEDA funding.
incentives.value_known: EDD example for Project Jupiter: $478M GRT share on $17B of construction

dockets.id: PRC large-load policy report (no case number found)
dockets.utility: PNM, El Paso Electric, Southwestern Public Service
dockets.what: PRC 2026 technical report on large-load tariffs for data centers. Per news, PNM plans to file a large-load tariff with minimum revenue requirements and exit fees, El Paso Electric proposed two large-load tariffs in its NM rate review, and the PRC will start a working group. Case numbers not found.

laws_and_bills.name: SB 235 (2026) Microgrid Oversight Act
laws_and_bills.what: Would have given the PRC oversight of large private microgrids such as Project Jupiter's. Passed Senate 22-20 on 2026-02-14; postponed indefinitely in House Judiciary.

laws_and_bills.name: Proposed statewide data center moratorium (for 2027 session)
laws_and_bills.what: Rep. Micaela Lara Cadena, Sen. Carrie Hamblen and Reps. Eleanor Chávez and Angelica Rubio outlined a bill for a statewide moratorium on large data centers. Not yet filed; no bill number. Also covered by KRQE: https://www.krqe.com/news/politics-government/two-new-mexico-lawmakers-outline-bill-for-possible-statewide-data-center-moratorium/

local_rules.what: One-year moratorium on data centers and related infrastructure on unincorporated land; advisory committee to recommend rules. Adopted unanimously.
18-month moratorium on new data centers drawing 1 MW or more. Passed unanimously.
18-month moratorium on future data center development, prompted by a Spaceport America proposal. Passed unanimously.
Commission approved a notice of intent to consider a one-year data center moratorium modeled on Socorro's; text to be weighed Oct 8, 2026.
local_rules.status: pending: final text was set for Oct 8, 2026; KRWG on Oct 14 still described the county as considering it, expected at the next commission meeting (Oct 22)

local_rules.what: 90-day emergency moratorium (Jan 12, 2026), extended twice through Sept 20, 2026; then Ordinance 2026-08-13 adopted Aug 10, 2026 amending the Unified Development Code with data center classes by electric demand, location limits, 100-200 ft buffers and noise limits.
City leaders postponed a vote on a temporary data center moratorium until after the Atterix feasibility study.
County government was considering a data center moratorium (reported alongside the Grant County Hachita proposal).
local_rules.status: under consideration (as of 2026-09-09); outcome not checked

local_rules.what: Town began considering a data center moratorium; Planning and Zoning Commission endorsed it. No data center proposal in town.
